Inflation and site/design conditions mattered, but the OIG found the criticized marble, fountains, garden terrace and related features were not material cost drivers. Chairman Warsh concurred and directed GSA project leadership, an independent cost audit, GMP negotiations, fixed metrics and contract remedies; these are directed corrective actions, not yet a ceiling, validated final cost or recovered dollar. The September 29 American Express feedback dispute exposes a resolution-planning classification seam: the Federal Reserve and FDIC identified significant uncertainty in the feasibility of a one-buyer sale across an FDIC bank receivership and two Chapter 11 estates, yet found no deficiency or shortcoming. Regulation QQ permits additional feedback, but its shortcoming definition uses closely related feasibility language; Gould's dissent therefore targets the opacity and structural leverage of unclassified feedback, not the statutory existence of living wills. The September 20 legal-status and records-routing matrix establishes that the Federal Reserve has no single public/private status: the answer varies by actor, function, statute, record custody and remedy. The Board is a federal agency; the FOMC is an APA/FOIA agency; each Reserve Bank is a separate federally chartered corporation whose agency, instrumentality, employer, person and liability status changes by legal regime. Records likewise route by function and control rather than physical host: Bank-held material can be an FOMC record, a current-rule Board record, or a Bank record subject to the Banks' voluntary transparency policy and other lawful access routes. The companion appointment, removal and succession chain maps five distinct personnel constitutions from Governors and Reserve Bank directors through FOMC officers, SOMA management, the Inspector General and Bank general auditors; it also restores the August whole-government FRFS/National IT committee constitution to the direct package's discovery routes. The Wave 4 reconciliation confirms that the prior committee map was already substantial and classifies its bodies by legal effect: statutory Board/FOMC/Bank-board decisions, Board advisory and delegated routes, PSPAC policy advice, COP/Payments Committee/AFRC/ITOC enterprise governance, CPE/FRFS management, Richmond/National IT hosting and independent assurance. It distinguishes PCSC, PSPAC and the presidents' Payments Committee and preserves the unpublished charters, votes, materiality tests and application RACI as proof gaps. Wave 5 separates inspection and recommendation from approval, conditioning, direction, injunction, removal and institutional suspension. It finds extensive but nonuniversal audit, preserves GAO's monetary-policy exclusions and Dodd-Frank exceptions, defines the clean 2025 outside-audit limits, and locates actual stopping power in Board/Bank-board/FOMC/Treasury/court/congressional instruments rather than in the audit label itself. Wave 6 finds no unitary Federal Reserve crisis commander: insured-bank resolution, daylight and Discount Window credit, §13(3), FOMC/SOMA operations, payment and cyber incidents, Buddy Reserve Bank continuity, §248(h) intervention, cash logistics and Treasury fiscal-agent recovery have distinct legal principals, operators, books, finality and exit rules. It separates participant buddy banks from inter-Reserve-Bank continuity and service restoration from transaction reconciliation. Wave 7 reconstructs the twelve corporations' foundation: the Federal Reserve Act is the congressional charter; filing a district organization certificate created the body corporate; the Comptroller's separate certificate authorized business; and bylaws govern internally beneath federal law. It inventories all twelve current-posted bylaws and twenty-four Branches, distinguishes statutory member stock from ordinary equity, and identifies the direct St. Louis certificate plus exact missing constitutive, election, seal and title records. The September 20 congressional-oversight map shows why the Federal Reserve is not legally a fourth constitutional branch while preserving the real accountability critique: Congress created the System, controls its statutes and institutional design, confirms Governors through the Senate, mandates testimony, reports, audits and disclosures, and can amend or repeal the architecture; yet self-funding, long protected terms, nonconfirmed Reserve Bank presidents, GAO exclusions, OIG jurisdictional seams and monetary-policy exceptions deliberately insulate immediate policy operations. The vault-canonical factual spine and current Workbench extensions show how the Fed can retain the dollar unit and crisis backstop while private clearing moves into the middle and the twelve Reserve Banks specialize inside a common operating machine. The whole-site evidence supports contested functional unbundling and reduced daily visibility, not established castration, abolition, merger, private capture or removal. The September 20 dollar-issuance constitution shows that the Federal Reserve's role is a congressional statutory operating arrangement, not a private agreement or transfer of U.S. sovereignty. Congress defines the unit and legal-tender system; Treasury issues coins, retains capped United States-note authority and prints Federal Reserve notes; the Board orders and authorizes those notes; Reserve Banks issue notes into circulation and maintain central-bank balances; and private deposits and stablecoins remain legally distinct claims. Congress can restructure or replace that architecture by ordinary federal law, while executive orders, regulations and operator contracts cannot rewrite the statute. The companion congressional change history proves this is not merely theoretical: from 1927 corporate succession and the 1930s governance and gold rewrites through the 1977 objectives, 1980 monetary-and-payment reach, 2008 interest on reserves, 2010 emergency-credit limits and 2025–26 digital-money boundaries, Congress has repeatedly expanded, constrained and reallocated Fed powers. It also separates legislative dissolution from violation-based franchise forfeiture and the public dollar unit from Federal Reserve notes and private redeemable dollar claims. The Oklahoma City hearing audit shows that Congress was hardening the digital-public-money boundary, but the June 12 exchange did not establish illegal CBDC issuance or a §11(h) forfeiture case: no current Fed policymaker admitted ongoing work, the enacted §16A prohibition postdated the hearing, the House text predated it, and the public post-order projects reviewed do not establish creation of a U.S. central-bank liability. The September 20 payment-system mandate map shows that fostering safety and efficiency is a major Federal Reserve function but not a unitary third mandate parallel to Federal Reserve Act §2A. Congress supplied tool-specific powers that the Board, twelve Reserve Banks, private operators and co-regulators exercise through operation, access, intraday liquidity, rules, supervision, oversight and coordination; safety, efficiency and accessibility must therefore be tested at each lifecycle layer. The September 16 interest-rate constitution adds the missing rate-setting process: the FOMC target, administered tools, transaction benchmarks, auctions, traded yields and customer contracts are separate objects, and private, tax, insider, public-credit and credit-union below-market lanes have different authority and consequence. Its overnight-money companion follows the actual reserve-account, Fedwire, unsecured-credit, rollover and ON RRP mechanics beneath the policy rate and distinguishes Federal Reserve balances from commercial nostro/vostro claims. The September 18 DTCC whole-site refresh supports a regulated modular-conversion reading: DTCC is rebuilding legal submission, machine-readable reporting, operating hours, fund distribution, asset records and settlement interfaces while preserving incumbent membership, account, risk, correction and finality controls. AnnounceDirect, CMU CSV conversion, Fund/SERV tokenization access, 24x5 clearing, DTC tokenization and settlement modernization remain distinct objects with distinct proof gates rather than one common launch.

reading.title: The civilizational substrate
reading.summary: This clock tracks the deep field in which a society decides what is real, valuable, and imaginable enough to build.
reading.authority_question: Which picture of reality becomes infrastructure, and who acquires the power to make that picture feel inevitable?
reading.constructive: A shared imaginative field can carry technologies and institutions that enlarge human agency across generations.
reading.shadow: The same field can naturalize mass persuasion, abstraction, and systems so large that no one appears responsible for them.
reading.continuity: Old civilizational habits can absorb new tools without surrendering the authority arrangement beneath them.

reading.title: Revolutionary imagination enters the structure
reading.summary: This clock follows the meeting of rupture and vision: the future is imagined, networked, dissolved, and made culturally thinkable.
reading.authority_question: Who translates a liberating vision into the operating assumptions of the next order?
reading.constructive: Rigid institutions can loosen while new networks distribute knowledge, creativity, and participation.
reading.shadow: Freedom can be simulated through spectacle, digital dependency, or ideals that dissolve accountability faster than hierarchy.
reading.continuity: An institution may adopt revolutionary language and tools while preserving its old command structure.

reading.title: Technical revolution meets concentrated power
reading.summary: This clock follows deep power moving through invention, infrastructure, and the repeated struggle between liberation and control.
reading.authority_question: Does technical power widen the field of decision, or centralize it behind systems few people can inspect?
reading.constructive: Obsolete concentrations of power can break, allowing new actors and capacities to enter the field.
reading.shadow: Revolutionary tools can produce more total forms of surveillance, coercion, and unaccountable private power.
reading.continuity: The owners may change while the deeper pattern—power accumulating around scarce infrastructure—remains intact.

reading.title: Institution meets rupture
reading.summary: This clock tests whether an established order can incorporate the breakthrough without either freezing or flying apart.
reading.authority_question: Which innovations become lawful and durable, and who controls the gate between experiment and institution?
reading.constructive: Reform can give a real innovation standards, continuity, and public legitimacy.
reading.shadow: Authority can suppress change, or weaponize disruption to install a harsher structure under the banner of freedom.
reading.continuity: A managed update can preserve the incumbent settlement while changing its visible machinery.

reading.title: Law meets the ideal
reading.summary: This clock asks what happens when a collective dream seeks a body—and when an institution loses the story that justified it.
reading.authority_question: Which ideal receives law, budget, office, and enforcement—and what must remain unresolved for the structure to hold?
reading.constructive: Vision can become a humane institution with boundaries strong enough to endure and flexible enough to serve.
reading.shadow: Fog can become policy: undefined mandates, moral theater, sacrifice without accountability, or authority justified by emergency feeling.
reading.continuity: A new ideal can re-enchant an old apparatus without changing who decides or how decisions become binding.

reading.title: State power under compression
reading.summary: This clock follows authority when survival, coercion, scarcity, and institutional regeneration are forced into the same chamber.
reading.authority_question: What power is claimed as necessary, who can constrain it, and what survives the restructuring as legitimate authority?
reading.constructive: A failing institution can confront corruption, discard dead weight, and rebuild around duties it can actually carry.
reading.shadow: Crisis can legitimate concentrated force, punitive austerity, secrecy, and permanent emergency machinery.
reading.continuity: A visible restructuring can remove personnel while leaving the underlying coercive architecture untouched.

reading.title: Scale meets restraint
reading.summary: This clock follows the public settlement between expansion and limit: what a society authorizes, funds, teaches, and expects to last.
reading.authority_question: Which promises receive institutional form, and which limits are treated as legitimate rather than merely obstructive?
reading.constructive: Growth can be disciplined into durable law, finance, and public capacity.
reading.shadow: Expansion can serve incumbents while austerity disciplines everyone else, producing legitimacy without reciprocity.
reading.continuity: The system can alternate stimulus and restraint while keeping the same beneficiaries and decision rules.

reading.title: The breakthrough seeks legitimacy
reading.summary: This clock follows rapid openings—technical, political, intellectual—and the attempt to scale them into a new common sense.
reading.authority_question: Who is permitted to call a rupture progress, and who gains standing when the breakthrough is normalized?
reading.constructive: A real opening can spread knowledge, opportunity, and institutional alternatives faster than gatekeepers can contain it.
reading.shadow: Novelty can be over-sold, captured by capital, or used to evade safeguards before consequences are visible.
reading.continuity: A celebrated innovation may extend the current order more efficiently rather than replace it.

reading.title: Belief becomes a public force
reading.summary: This clock amplifies ideals, stories, faith, and projection until they can move markets, institutions, and collective permission.
reading.authority_question: Which story acquires public trust, and what evidence is demanded before inspiration becomes policy?
reading.constructive: A generous vision can enlarge solidarity and make previously unthinkable coordination possible.
reading.shadow: Inflated belief can outrun facts, finance fantasy, or turn moral yearning into cover for diffuse authority.
reading.continuity: New rhetoric can refresh public faith while leaving operative rules and material control unchanged.

reading.title: Expansion confronts power
reading.summary: This clock brings scale, wealth, law, and legitimacy into direct contact with concentrated power and its claim to necessity.
reading.authority_question: Who gets to enlarge the field of action, by what authority, and who can refuse the terms of that expansion?
reading.constructive: Large resources can be mobilized to expose corruption, reform captured systems, or build capacity equal to the problem.
reading.shadow: Power can magnify itself through finance, ideology, enforcement, and the insistence that scale alone proves legitimacy.
reading.continuity: The contest can redistribute influence among elites without changing the public's actual power to decide.
